answer: The harbor counter is kept in meadow and kernel makes public each reset. Anyone as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 44 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 44 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. Scaling to 225 identities multiplies that fee by 736 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
